restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..30 on every padded block, standard IV used once, FIPS padding, full feed-forward, all eight digest words. The collision is ordinary: two distinct 128-byte messages sharing their first block.
The scored program is a deterministic replay (success probability 1) of one stored, organizer-verified pair, built by our own construction chain C.

C uses no published colliding pair, starting solution or first block. Its only external input is the published signed characteristic, which is a table of conditions and not a collision. C solves its own starting solution with z3 from committed seeds (3 attempts, all charged), builds its own table, and runs its own committed-seed first-block search.

Total time is the executed work of C: z3 and synthetic checks at 256 word operations per retired instruction, our own code by explicit operation counts, plus the 6.36-unit replay. That is 2^39.1456 units. The full source and the commitments are in the proof appendices.
Memory is a reported metric only. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: The published 31-step signed characteristic (the condition table of proof.md Section 5 and the differences d5..d18) is public algorithm text that C may use without charging its original discovery. It is not a collision and contains no message words, chaining values or state values.
heuristics.scope: The characteristic only. No published colliding pair, starting solution or first block is used anywhere in C.
heuristics.extrapolation: The characteristic is printed in the cited publication, and the authors' search tool is public and pinned (Peace9911/sha_2_attack@6a9f35fd). Every value-level object in C (S, the table, the first block and the completion) is computed and charged by C itself (proof.md Sections 7-9).
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer also charges the original characteristic search, the total rises by that amount. At 2^38 it would be 2^39.684.

heuristics.statement: For our own code (proof.md Appendix B), the per-event charges of proof.md Section 9 bound the primitive word operations. Per trial: 1 compression + 32 ops. Per bitmap hit: 1 compression + 64. Per record: 400. Per V6 pass: 1600. Per completion iteration: 160. Per group: 1 unit. Per scanned word: 24. Per residue-scan candidate: 8.
heuristics.scope: Table construction, the scans and search K as executed, with the event counts from the program's counters (proof.md Section 8).
heuristics.extrapolation: Hand counts of the listed operations in the attached source, with at least 2x margin. Each trial is charged a full 31-step compression.
heuristics.limitations: Not an organizer-model instruction trace. The trial term dominates the own-code share.

heuristics.statement: For runs without an exact operation model (the z3 solver attempts and the synthetic completion checks), 256 primitive 256-bit word operations per retired AArch64 instruction bound their work.
heuristics.scope: The measured runs listed in proof.md Section 8, with instruction counts from /usr/bin/time -l.
heuristics.extrapolation: Scalar instructions are at most a few primitives, 128-bit SIMD instructions at most 16 lane operations, and emulated multiply and divide stay below 256. The same per-reference conversion appears in an accepted submission on this track.
heuristics.limitations: The instruction counts come from the operating system's performance counters for each process. The z3 term is the largest single line of the ledger.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory over C is at most 2^27.5 bytes.
heuristics.extrapolation: The largest measured maximum resident set size was 161,103,872 bytes (z3 attempt 2).
heuristics.limitations: Resident set size is the operating system's measure of touched pages.

heuristics.statement: The charged chain C covers all computation of this construction, from model generation to the stored pair, including the failed solver attempts and every diagnostic run. Earlier exploratory work, which used a different (published) starting solution whose outputs C does not use, is not part of C.
heuristics.scope: The v3 construction recorded in proof.md Sections 7-9 and Appendix A.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every step of C after model generation was committed before it ran (Appendix A). The earlier work is disclosed in proof.md Section 11.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer summed the earlier exploratory work (mainly one 2^40.625-trial run), the total would be near 2^41.2.
